newsitem.title: UK: BOE not confident time ripe for single regulator.
newsitem.headline: BOE not confident time ripe for single regulator.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Wednesday he was not confident the time was ripe for a single, over-arching financial regulator for the City of London.
George told a news conference it had long been clear that changes in the financial markets were causing traditional distinctions between banks and other financial institutions to become blurred.
That process would require a single regulator at some point. "But we're not confident that point has been reached now," he said.
George said he did not disagree with the broad principle of a single regulator.
"It's a world we're moving towards, even if we're not there yet," he said, adding: "But the implementation is going to be hugely difficult."
Banks were still special "in a systemic sense", providing liquidity to both depositors and borrowers.
George added that the Bank of England could not be shut out of the regulatory process.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Tuesday unveiled sweeping plans to overhaul regulation of the financial services industry.

Brown will transfer responsibility for supervising banks from the Bank of England to a strengthened Securities and Investment Board, which will regulate all banks, securities firms and insurance companies.
